dedupe_keys.name: stuttgart ventilation corridors and green blue infrastructure against heat and air pollution

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Stuttgart, Germany, which lies in the Neckar valley basin with low wind speeds, heavy traffic and a strong urban heat island, uses its Climate Atlas of 2008, built on work by the city's urban climatology department (in place since 1938), to steer zoning and land-use planning. Standardised climate assessments map cold air production areas and ventilation paths from the hills to the valley floor; planning keeps these corridors open, protects open space and steep vineyards, and expands parks, street trees, green roofs and water features. Coverage is the city and the Stuttgart region. Since 2016 the city has given about 2 million euros a year for greening, 12.7 million euros once for park renovation and about 850,000 euros a year in 2018-2021 for slopes and vineyards; no total cost estimate exists. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the online Climate Atlas. Caveats: effects on temperature and air quality are not quantified on the page, and implementation through land-use planning takes years. It illustrates the use of urban climate analysis and green and blue infrastructure for climate adaptation and heat hazard reduction; related records are the Copernicus Urban Atlas, ERA5 and the Berlin Biotope Area Factor case study.
name: Stuttgart ventilation corridors and green-blue infrastructure against heat and air pollution
outcomes: Decades of climate-informed zoning have preserved ventilation corridors and open space and expanded greening, supported by annual greening budgets since 2016.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the City of Stuttgart and the GRaBS project
